notes: Changed rule, graded against the current text: Chain fallible steps with `with`. The rule now opens "A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`." and its one-step paragraph reads "Count the `<-` clauses before writing `with`. With one there is nothing to chain, and a `with` makes the reader look for the other steps, so use `case`, which shows both outcomes in one place. When the body of a one-step `with` calls another function that can fail, that call is the second step: chain it with a second `<-` instead of nesting a `case` or adding an `else`." (SKILL.md, under the rule heading). One-step sentence: 0 of 4 runs violate (no with has a single `<-`: haiku-1 lines 157-158 has two steps, sonnet-1 lines 160-161 and 206-209 have two and four, sonnet-2 lines 170-172 has three, and haiku-2 has no with and uses case at lines 103 and 149). Else sentence, unchanged: 0 of 4 runs violate. Three calls decided these counts. Sonnet-1's init/1 with ends in else / {:error, reason} -> {:stop, reason} (lines 174-175); it keeps each step's reason and only rewraps it as the tuple init/1 must return, mapping nothing back to a step, and the first batch cited the same else in its haiku-1 (lines 132-133) only under the one-step sentence, so it is not counted. Haiku-1's with chains File.read/1 and Jason.decode/1 directly with no private step functions and no else; both already return {:ok, value} or {:error, reason} and the errors pass through unchanged, so it is not counted. Haiku-2's load_limits/1 (lines 149-152) is a case whose :ok branch calls a second fallible function, validate_limits/1; the second-step sentence speaks of a one-step with, so it is not counted, though a two-step with would state the chain more directly. In the first batch both Haiku runs violated both sentences (2 of 4 each); here neither does.

Changed rule, graded against the current text as in the first batch: Naming. Fetch sentence ("A function that looks a key up and also checks the value, returning `{:error, reason}`, is not a `fetch`: name it by its job, such as `string_field/2` or `parse_amount/1`."): 1 of 4 runs violates, sonnet-1, whose fetch_limit/2 (lines 229-232) looks up "default", checks is_integer(limit) and limit > 0, and returns {:error, {:invalid_limit, "default"}}. Generic-name sentence (now adding "A variable may carry the name of the external key it holds, as in `%{"data" => data}`, since the payload chose that name."): 0 of 4 runs violate; no run uses data, item, res, x or a single-letter name. Sonnet-1's acc in a reduce_while accumulator (line 236) was not counted, as before, and haiku-1's ts for a request timestamp (line 149) was not counted because it abbreviates a domain term. Other Naming sentences: 0 of 4 (every module is under MyApp, and no run defines a boolean-returning or get-named function).

All four runs read the limits file inside init/1 (haiku-1 line 102, File.read at line 157; haiku-2 line 103, :file.consult at line 149; sonnet-1 lines 160-161, File.read at line 215; sonnet-2 line 118, File.read at line 178). The responsive rule is unchanged and names only HTTP calls and large queries as slow work, so as in the first batch no verdict rests on it, but every run misses the case's init check. All four start_link/1 functions accept :name (haiku-1 line 74, haiku-2 line 68, sonnet-1 lines 101-102, sonnet-2 line 84), and in a scratch run each started a second instance under name: :other. In the first batch haiku-2 lacked :name, so the responsive rule is now clean in all four runs.

All four runs keep counts in an ETS table owned by the GenServer and write it from the caller with insert-then-count, so Pick the abstraction and Use ETS are clean in all four, as in the first batch. Branching, Comments and the five process rules are unchanged and graded to the first batch's standard. Sonnet-1's section labels (## Client, ## Server, ## Config loading at lines 84, 156, 189) and the missing @doc on its example worker's perform/1 (line 257) were not counted, as the previous sweep did not count the same in baseline-sonnet-1 for this case.

Each file was formatted, compiled and run in a scratch copy. All four pass mix format --check-formatted. Haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 compile with no warnings. Haiku-1 warns that Jason.decode/1 is undefined because Jason is not installed (the session compiled against a stub; the built-in JSON.decode/1 would avoid it), which the previous sweep recorded as a note, not a violation. Each run admitted exactly 2 of a 50-task burst at a limit of 2, and each sweep removed an expired row and kept a fresh one. In haiku-2 a string user ID in the term file loads as a charlist and never matches, so its documented {"svc-backfill", 600}. entry has no effect; this is a correctness defect, not a graded rule.
